Sealing that holds under pressure and chemistry.
Hydrocarbon service is unforgiving. Compound selection is driven by the media, service temperature and pressure class of your application, not by catalogue availability.
FKM compounds resist petroleum oils, fuels and many solvents at sustained temperature — the default for aggressive process media. NBR where contact is moderate-temperature oil.
Compounds selected across the full service envelope: FKM to +250 °C, silicone from −60 °C, EPDM from −40 °C — sub-zero ambient through to sustained high-temperature process duty.
Geometry and hardness chosen for repeated pressure cycling rather than static sealing alone. Back-up rings specified where extrusion gap and pressure require them.
Sealed geometries maintain integrity in particulate-laden, wet and corrosive atmospheres typical of process plant.

Which compounds do you recommend for hydrocarbon service?

FKM is the usual choice where petroleum oils, fuels or solvents are present at sustained temperature, rated to +250 °C. NBR suits moderate-temperature oil contact to +120 °C. EPDM is specified for water, steam and desalination duty but must not be used in petroleum service. Send your media, service temperature and pressure class and we will confirm the compound and hardness.
